title.description: Paper title exactly as it appears on the title page.

authors.description: Comma-separated author list. Use '*' to mark equal contribution if the paper does. Do not invent affiliations.

affiliation.description: Comma-separated affiliations as listed in the paper.

conference.description: Full conference name + year, e.g. 'International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR) 2026'. If the paper appears to be an ICLR 2026 submission, write that.

pdf_pages.description: Total page count of the PDF including references and appendix.

page_count_range.description: [min, max] slide count, typically [16, 20] for an oral presentation. Pick a range appropriate to the paper's depth.

central_thesis.description: One sentence: problem the paper addresses, the method/approach, and the headline result or tradeoff. Avoid vague verbs like 'studies' or 'investigates'.

ordered_sections.description: Ordered slide sections that will become Section 1 of instructions.md. Must include title, outline, intro/background, limitations of existing methods, method overview, methodology, key algorithm or training details, datasets, experimental setup, results, takeaways/limitations, and conclusion. May include one or more visual_analysis sections.

title.description: Section heading as it should appear, e.g. 'Methodology: Camera-Ray Conversion'. Make it paper-specific, not 'Methodology'.

bullets.description: For non-title sections: 2-5 short bullets in 'Label: qualitative claim' form, each <=25 words, describing WHAT TOPIC the slide must cover and the qualitative framing to highlight (e.g. 'Core Idea: Recast pose inference as patch-wise ray prediction, treating a camera as a bundle of rays represented in Plücker coordinates.'). Bullets must be paper-specific at the topic / mechanism / dataset / baseline-name level so they cannot be swapped into another paper unchanged. Bullets must NOT include: specific numerical results (accuracy %, mAP, EM, CIDEr, BLEU, F1, ROUGE, METEOR, scores, ratios); baseline-vs-baseline numerical rankings; '+/-Δ' improvement values; module dimensions paired with their effect; '±std' noise; the verbatim 'correct_form' of any trap. Those values live exclusively in key_numbers / key_terms / traps and flow only to the Stage 3 rubric — the slide-generating model is supposed to retrieve them from the PDF and earn credit for putting them on the slides. For title section: provide four bullets exactly: 'Paper Title: ...', 'Author Team: ...', 'Affiliation: ...', 'Conference: ...'. For outline section: empty array.

design_constraint.description: Optional. Cite WHICH figure/table the slide must display and WHAT TOPIC it shows — never a specific value. Form: 'Display <Fig X> showing <topical description>' or 'Include <Table Y> comparing <baselines/metrics topically>' (e.g. 'Display the conversion process diagram (refer to Fig 2) showing the flow between traditional camera parameters and Plücker rays.'). Do NOT embed specific numerical results, accuracy values, or '+/-Δ' improvements in this line — those are answers the slide-generation model must retrieve from the PDF. Methodology, results, and visual analysis sections SHOULD include one. At least 3 sections in the deck must carry a design_constraint.

key_numbers.description: Quantities the deck must report accurately. Each entry is a self-contained anchor for a correctness checklist item.

claim.description: Full claim including value, unit, and condition, e.g. 'rotation accuracy below 15° on unseen CO3D categories with 8 input views'.

key_figures.description: Figures or tables that must be reproduced or cited in the deck.

id.description: As labeled in the paper, e.g. 'Fig 2', 'Table 1'.

what.description: What the figure or table shows.

intended_slide.description: Which ordered_section this figure should appear on, by its title or kind.

key_terms.description: Defined terms or concepts the paper introduces that the deck must define correctly. Each anchors a correctness checklist item.

common_confusion.description: Optional. The plausible-but-wrong claim a careless deck might make.

traps.description: Specific risks of inaccurate framing the deck must avoid. Used to generate the most discriminative correctness checklist items.

claim_to_avoid.description: The wrong claim to flag, in concrete words.

correct_form.description: The faithful form supported by the paper.

language_note.description: Optional one-line note on language, e.g. 'paper is in English'. The output task is always English regardless.

pages_read.description: Which pages were read, e.g. '1-12 (full)' or '1-6, 9-11'.
